title: Multilingual Severity Mapping and Customer Notice Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines how Redwood sends customer-facing notifications and internal incident triage guidance for SLO degradations and outages across English, Spanish, and French-speaking customers. It includes a clear severity mapping, templated notices for status pages, email, and support tickets, automated payload examples for our status API, and guidance for reviewers/translators to preserve legal and SLA language.

Scope:
- Applies to all customer-impacting incidents in Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private control plane communications where customer-facing notices are required.
- Focused on service availability, latency SLO regressions, and data plane degradations.
- Not intended for regulatory/legal notices; engage Security & Legal when disclaimers are required.

Goals:
- Reduce confusion by standardizing severity labels and message tone across languages.
- Ensure timely, consistent customer updates (initial, update, resolution).
- Provide automation-ready templates to minimize manual translation errors during incidents.

Definitions:
- Severity P0 (Sev0): Total outage for a cohort of customers or Redwood control plane — immediate bridge and executive notification.
- Severity P1 (Sev1): Significant SLO breach (availability < 95% or latency 3x baseline for 30+ mins) affecting many customers.
- Severity P2 (Sev2): Partial impact (single region, degraded performance, or tiered degradation) with mitigations available.
- Severity P3 (Sev3): Minor or single-tenant issues, scheduled maintenance, or informational only.

Severity-to-Communication Mapping (at-a-glance):
| Severity | Time-to-first-notice | Channels | Customer-level action | Status cadence |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| P0 | 10 minutes | Status page, Email, Customer CS, Public Slack, Executive bridge | Immediate mitigation; credits discussion | Every 10–15m until stable |
| P1 | 30 minutes | Status page, Support ticket update, CS outreach | Suggested workarounds; canary routing | Every 30–60m |
| P2 | 60 minutes | Status page, Support ticket | Monitoring & advisory; escalation if worsens | Every 2–4 hours |
| P3 | On next business day | Status page postmortem | Informational | Final report upon closure |

Ownership and Run-to-Completion Steps (Incident Commander checklist):
1. Confirm severity level using SLO tooling (SLO dashboard, error-rate graphs, region filters).
2. Open incident bridge and tag the locales impacted.
3. Trigger automated status page draft creation (see API example below).
4. Assign a communicator (CS or Ops) to post initial notice and coordinate translations.
5. Post the initial notice in English, then produce translated notices within the next update window (see translation guidance).
6. Update cadence per severity mapping until resolution.
7. Complete post-incident report and attach final customer notification in all languages.

Automation: status API example (curl):
- Create draft status update (replace API_KEY and INCIDENT_ID):
```
curl -X POST \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  https://status.redwood.ai/api/incidents/$INCIDENT_ID/updates \
  -d '{"state":"investigating","body":{"en":"{EN_NOTICE}","es":"{ES_NOTICE}","fr":"{FR_NOTICE}"},"visibility":"public"}'
```
Notes: use JSON-safe escaped strings when injecting templates. The body object contains localized payloads keyed by ISO language codes.

Translation guidance (fast, accurate, and safe):
- Primary message must be composed in English first. Identify required legal/SLA phrases to avoid rewording.
- Use in-house translation pool (Customer Success + localized SREs) where possible. If external translators are used, set trust level = reviewer_required.
- Preserve numeric and SLA terms verbatim (e.g., "99.9% SLA" -> always displayed as-is).
- Avoid idioms and slang in customer-facing notices. Use neutral, professional tone.

Templates: initial, update, and resolution (English / Spanish / French)
- Initial notice (EN):
Subject: Incident: Degraded API performance in {region} — investigating
Body: We are aware of increased latency and error rates for API requests in {region}. Our engineers are investigating the issue. We will provide an update within {update_window}. Customers may experience delayed responses or timeouts.
- Initial notice (ES):
Asunto: Incidente: Rendimiento degradado de la API en {region} — investigando
Cuerpo: Hemos detectado un aumento de latencia y errores en las solicitudes de la API en {region}. Nuestros ingenieros están investigando. Publicaremos una actualización en {update_window}. Es posible que los clientes experimenten respuestas retrasadas o errores de tiempo de espera.
- Initial notice (FR):
Objet: Incident: performance dégradée de l'API dans {region} — en cours d'investigation
Corps: Nous constatons une augmentation de la latence et des taux d'erreur pour les requêtes API dans {region}. Nos ingénieurs enquêtent. Nous publierons une mise à jour dans {update_window}. Les clients peuvent rencontrer des réponses retardées ou des timeouts.

- Update notice pattern (concise):
EN: Update: Investigating root cause; mitigation (if any); ETA for next update.
ES: Actualización: Investigando la causa raíz; mitigación (si aplica); ETA para la próxima actualización.
FR: Mise à jour: Enquête sur la cause; atténuation (le cas échéant); ETA pour la prochaine mise à jour.

- Resolution notice: include cause summary, mitigations applied, customer impact, credits (if any), and link to postmortem.

Support ticket template (to attach to customer tickets):
- Subject: Incident {INCIDENT_ID} — impact to API in {region} — {resolved/ongoing}
- Body (EN): We encountered elevated error rates affecting {subset}. Our team applied {mitigation} at {timestamp}. If you continue to see issues, please reply with the last request ID and timestamp.

Example translated message payload (JSON snippet for automation):
{
  "incident_id": "INC-2026-1234",
  "update_type": "initial",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "body": {
    "en": "We are aware of increased latency...",
    "es": "Hemos detectado un aumento de latencia...",
    "fr": "Nous constatons une augmentation de la latence..."
  }
}

Escalation matrix (roles and contact cadence):
- On-call engineer (first 30–60m): troubleshooting and first mitigation steps.
- SRE lead (30–90m for P1/P0): architecture and failover decisions.
- Customer Success lead (immediately for P0/P1): customer notifications and prioritized outreach.
- Head of Product / VP Eng (P0 brief within 30m).

Localization quality checklist (for communicator to tick off in bridge):
- [ ] Numeric values and SLAs unchanged.
- [ ] No ambiguous pronouns or unclear remediation steps.
- [ ] Translation reviewed by native-speaker reviewer.
- [ ] Legal/KMS/PII language preserved if present.

Game-day exercises and validation:
- Run quarterly drills that inject a simulated P1 in a specific region and require the on-call team to post initial bilingual notices within the SLA.
- Measurement: time-to-first-notice (target < 30m), translation availability (< 15m after English post), automated status API success rate (> 99%).

Operational examples and quick-reference snippets:
- Populate variable placeholders with the incident automation tool: {region}, {update_window}, {incident_id}, {mitigation}, {timestamp}.
- Use the following jq filter to confirm localized keys before sending:
```
cat payload.json | jq '.body | keys'  # should include ["en","es","fr"]
```

Escalation: when to use legal and external comms teams:
- Engage Security & Legal immediately if customer data exposure is suspected.
- Engage Legal/PR for any P0 that has external regulatory implications or may require press statements.

Appendix: recommended tone examples and forbidden phrases
- Recommended: "We are investigating and will update by {time}. We understand the impact and are prioritizing a fix."
- Forbidden: absolutes and speculative statements such as "service fully restored" before verification, or "no customer data was exposed" without Security sign-off.

Appendix B: Quick translator cheat-sheet
- Keep subject lines short and verbatim between languages where possible.
- For Spanish: prefer neutral Latin American Spanish (es) unless customer cohort tagged as es-ES.
- For French: use FR standard; avoid Canadian-specific spelling unless customer is in CA.

Related artifacts to produce at incident closure:
- Final multilingual resolution notice (same language set as initial).
- Postmortem with evidence links and timeline (attach to incident).
- Customer-specific follow-up for large enterprise customers (one-off translated Q&A).

Owner: Customer Success (incident communication), SRE (technical triage), Legal (as required).
